'''Pietro De Martino''' or '''Di Martino''' (31 May 1707 – 28 January 1746) was a [[mathematician]] and [[astronomer]] from the [[Kingdom of Naples]].<ref name="DBI">{{Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani|title=DE MARTINO, Pietro|author=Pietro Nastasi|year=1990|volume=38|url=https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/pietro-de-martino_(Dizionario-Biografico)}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Born in [[Faicchio]], he was the brother of Angelo, professor first of [[medical physics]] then of mathematics at the [[University of Naples]]; and of [[Nicola Antonio De Martino]], professor of mathematics and director of the Real Corpo degli Ingegneri (Royal Engineers Corp) and Marine Guard. Pietro De Martino was a pupil of [[Agostino Ariani]] and of Giacinto De Cristoforo (1650-1730). In 1735, he was assigned to the astronomical and nautical chair at the University of Naples.<ref name="inaf">{{Cite web|url=http://www.beniculturali.inaf.it/sicap/opac.aspx?WEB=INAFS&TBL=AST&ID=92|title=Pietro Di Martino|website=Stardust: the cultural heritage of Italian astronomy|last=Gargano|first=Mauro|year=2012|language=it|access-date=7 July 2017|archive-date=22 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201022094406/http://www.beniculturali.inaf.it/sicap/opac.aspx?WEB=INAFS&TBL=AST&ID=92|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He disputed with [[Roger Joseph Boscovich]] on the question if it is possible to gain a right result starting from a wrong [[hypothesis]].<ref name="DBI" />

He authored various works; his ''Nuove istituzioni di aritmetica pratica'', published originally in 1739 in Naples, had many reprints (the better known of the 1758; one also in [[Turin]] in 1762).<ref name="DBI" /> He died in Naples in 1746.<ref name="inaf" />
